reader.requirement: At --std 85 the RELATIVE KEY data-name-1 of the ACCESS MODE clause (SEQUENTIAL, RANDOM or DYNAMIC) must be accepted when written with IN/OF qualifiers (one or more levels, up to a file-name), resolved to the item the qualifiers select, and used as the relative key by the I-O statements; an unqualified non-unique or wrongly qualified name must be refused, and, data-name-1 being a data-name, a subscript is not admitted.

edition-consulted.switches: below 2002 the RELATIVE KEY clause must directly follow the ACCESS MODE clause (2002 F.2 item 112 freed it); qualification is untouched
EditionInfo.SubscriptedClauseOperands (true only at 2002): whether a subscript on the data-name operand is kept; at 85 it is refused, as at 2023
the 2002 occurrence screen; returns at once at 85 and 2023

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 the RELATIVE KEY phrase is part of the ACCESS MODE clause, so a free-standing RELATIVE KEY clause is refused (COBOL0900) and accepted at 2023; qualification behaves the same

reader.notes: Qualification goes through the one clause-operand capture (KeyReference) and resolution (ResolveClauseOperand) every edition shares. The 1985 placement of the phrase inside ACCESS MODE is a separate parse-arm gate. rkq1's sequential file keeps its key in another file's record area; that is legal (SR3 bars only the file's own records).
